title: Carrying his drums through the rain between record dates
summary: After a Joe Turner date at Fulton Studio he could not get a cab and walked his drums to Capitol Studio in the rain.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Well, that's unfortunate that that happened. Hey, what was your first car, man?

My first car -- and this is a funny story -- I did a recording date at Fulton Studio, that was the name of it at the time, at 40th Street and 6th Avenue. And I think, if I'm not mistaken, it was a date that I did with Joe Turner when I recorded "Corina Corina" with him. So I come downstairs, and it's beginning to rain, slightly. After awhile, it started coming down a little heavy, and I'm waving for the cabs, because at that time, I didn't have any wheels on my drum case or nothing, and the studio - they didn't start using bass drums or tom toms in the studio yet, so ...
Had to bring your own stuff?

You had to bring your own drums. So here I am standing on 6th Avenue, 40th Street, trying to get a cab, and they're passing me by like I wasn't there. So I got another date starting at 7 o'clock at Capital, which was like 6 -- almost 7 blocks away, and I got all these drums tocarry, and it's raining.

So I stood there and stood there, waving and waving, and I'm getting wet and the rain is getting harder, so I finally decided that I better do something -- so I took my bass drum, put it under my arm, and I took my tom toms and put that over my arm and with the drum case, and I picked it all up -- I don't know where I got the strength from -- but I picked all of this stuff up and walked from 40th Street to 46th Street, near Broadway to Capital Studio -- soaking wet.
